guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 35
A MAJOR PENTATONIC HORIZONTAL STRING LANES - CONTROLLED SHIFTS, SLIDES, AND DESTINATION LANDINGS
PURPOSE
Keep the key fixed as A major pentatonic and turn the five vertical positions from Level 34 into six
horizontal one-string melodies. First relocate silently between three two-note stations, then isolate one
timed slide at each of the four position seams, then land directly on named destinations over increasing
distances. Finish by linking all six strings in a forward and reverse horizontal snake.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
This level does not transpose the shape. Every note belongs to A major pentatonic: A B C# E F#.
The suggested route fingerings are designed for continuous one-string movement and therefore do not always
match the vertical-box fingerings from Level 34. The fret, note, degree, and timing are authoritative.
A MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
Notes:   A B C# E F#
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
HORIZONTAL LANE SUMMARY
Low E   frets 5 7 9 12 14 17     degrees 1 2 3 5 6 1  notes A B C# E F# A    fingers 1 3 1 4 1 4 roots 5,17
A       frets 4 7 9 12 14 16     degrees 3 5 6 1 2 3  notes C# E F# A B C#   fingers 1 4 1 4 1 3 roots 12
D       frets 4 7 9 11 14 16     degrees 6 1 2 3 5 6  notes F# A B C# E F#   fingers 1 4 1 3 1 3 roots 7
G       frets 4 6 9 11 14 16     degrees 2 3 5 6 1 2  notes B C# E F# A B    fingers 1 3 1 3 1 3 roots 14
B       frets 5 7 10 12 14 17    degrees 5 6 1 2 3 5  notes E F# A B C# E    fingers 1 3 1 3 1 4 roots 10
High e  frets 5 7 9 12 14 17     degrees 1 2 3 5 6 1  notes A B C# E F# A    fingers 1 3 1 4 1 4 roots 5,17
PICKING AND COUNT RULES
Module A: six 12-note picked cells = 72 picked notes.
Module B: 24 slide phrases x 6 sounding tones = 144 sounding tones, but only 96 pick attacks.
Module C: six 16-note destination ladders = 96 picked notes.
Module D: forward 36 + reverse 36 = 72 picked notes.
Complete Level 35 workout = 384 sounding tones / 336 pick attacks.
STRICT ALTERNATE PICKING
Complete separate D-start and U-start passes. Do not restart at a string change, station shift, seam slide,
repeated destination, A root, or forward/reverse turnaround. A slide destination is sounded without a new
pick attack and must arrive exactly on the subdivision.
MODULE A - SIX SILENT-SHIFT HORIZONTAL LANES
Group each lane into three two-note stations. Use finger 1-3 for a whole step and 1-4 for a minor third.
Shift after the first station and after the second station. Release pressure before moving. No slide is allowed.

txt_lines_1_40: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 36
A MAJOR PENTATONIC EXPRESSIVE ARTICULATION - LEGATO, SLIDES, BENDS, RELEASES, AND VIBRATO
FIXED KEY A - FIVE POSITIONS - FRETS 4-17
PURPOSE
Turn the fixed-key A-major-pentatonic map from Levels 34-35 into controlled expressive motion. The pitch map
does not change. What changes is how each pitch begins, connects, bends, releases, and sustains. Train hammer-ons
and pull-offs in all five positions, combine legato with the four shared-anchor seams, calibrate whole-step bends
against named target frets, add pre-bend releases and pitch-centered vibrato, then finish with five short cadences.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Expression does not excuse inaccurate rhythm or pitch. A hammer-on, pull-off, slide arrival, bend target, release,
or vibrato pulse is a timed musical event. Picked and unpicked notes must remain equal in volume and duration.
All core bends in this level are whole-step bends to a note two frets higher. The minor-third gaps 3->5 and 6->1
would require a one-and-a-half-step bend and are deliberately excluded from the core bend module.
A MAJOR PENTATONIC
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
ARTICULATION NOTATION
h = hammer-on; p = pull-off; / = ascending slide; \ = descending slide; b(T) = bend to target fret T;
r = release; pb(T) = pre-bend silently to target pitch before the attack; ~ = vibrato.
COUNTS
Module A: 5 position cells x 24 sounding tones = 120 tones; 12 attacks per cell = 60 attacks.
Module B: 4 seams x 6 strings x 5 tones = 120 tones; one attack per phrase = 24 attacks.
Module C: 9 whole-step bend sites x 4 attacks = 36 attacks.
Module D: 6 pre-bend cells x 3 attacks = 18 attacks; 8 A-root vibrato holds = 8 attacks.
Module E: 5 cadence phrases = 19 attacks; articulation creates the remaining pitch motion.
Complete core workout: 165 pick attacks, plus 240 explicitly counted legato/slide tones, 15 bend or pre-bend
cells, 8 root-vibrato holds, and 5 cadence phrases.
MODULE A - FIVE-POSITION LEGATO CELLS
Pick the first tone of each two-note group. Hammer the ascending partner and pull off the descending partner.
Each position contains 12 groups, 24 sounding tones, and 12 pick attacks. Alternate the group attacks continuously.
D-start groups: D U D U D U | D U D U D U. U-start groups: U D U D U D | U D U D U D.
txt_lines_200_206: MODULE D - PRE-BEND RELEASES AND PITCH-CENTERED VIBRATO
Pre-bend rule: reach the target pitch silently before attacking. The listener should hear the target first, then the
controlled release. The final bend reaches the same target and adds narrow vibrato only after the pitch is stable.
txt_lines_223_228: Vibrato passes: 4 pulses per whole note; 6 pulses per whole note; then free vibrato while returning to the
original pitch between pulses. On a bent note, reach the target first and vibrate around that target.
MODULE E - FIVE POSITION EXPRESSIVE CADENCES
txt_lines_279_324: Linking rule: practice each cadence alone, then play P1-P5 with one bar of rest between phrases. Finally remove
the rests. Continue alternate picking through the actual attacks; do not add an attack to a hammer, pull, slide,
bend arrival, release, or held vibrato note.
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Map the notation and say the A-major-pentatonic notes and degrees before playing.
2. Complete one Position 1 legato cell at one sounding tone per click.
3. Play all five Module A cells with both D-start and U-start attack cycles.
4. Add one seam page; keep all five tones equal from a single attack.
5. Calibrate one bend site by alternating the fretted target and bent target.
6. Complete all nine bend cells without overshooting, sagging, or adjacent-string noise.
7. Add pre-bend releases, then the eight A-root vibrato holds.
8. Play the five cadences separately, then link them without extra attacks.
ERROR DIAGNOSIS
WEAK HAMMER: strike closer to the fret with less travel; do not squeeze harder with the thumb.
EMPTY PULL-OFF: keep the destination fretted and use a tiny lateral pluck rather than simply lifting.
LATE SLIDE: shorten the motion; the arrival fret is a counted tone, not transportation.
FLAT BEND: support the bending finger, rotate the wrist, and compare directly with the target fret.
SHARP BEND: stop pushing after the target; hold the pitch before adding vibrato.
WIDE VIBRATO: reduce the motion until every pulse returns to the pitch center.
STRING NOISE: mute above the bend with the fretting index and below it with the picking hand.
PAIN OR TENSION: stop. Do not force the whole-step bend or substitute a one-and-a-half-step bend.
ADVANCEMENT RULES
Add 2 BPM after three clean runs at the current module length. After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or isolate one
string, seam, bend, or cadence. Intonation outranks speed. Use a clean tone until the pitch and muting are stable.
MASTERY GATE BEFORE LEVEL 37
Play all five legato cells with equal picked and unpicked volume; execute all 24 one-pick seam chains without an
extra attack; match all nine whole-step bends to their fretted targets; perform six pre-bend releases without a
scoop; hold all eight A roots with controlled vibrato; link the five cadence phrases on two separate days; and
identify the note and degree of every bend source, bend target, and final root.

treating every scale tone as equally stable.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 37
A MAJOR PENTATONIC I-IV-V CHORD-TONE TARGETING AND VOICE LEADING
FIXED KEY A - FIVE POSITIONS - A, D, AND E MAJOR HARMONY
PURPOSE
Turn the fixed-key A-major-pentatonic map into harmony-aware phrasing. Keep the same five notes and five positions,
but stop treating every note as equally stable. Hear the active I, IV, or V chord; land on a strong chord tone at
the change; use the remaining pentatonic notes as motion; then resolve before the harmony changes again.
A MAJOR PENTATONIC
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
I-IV-V chords: A major = A C# E; D major = D F# A; E major = E G# B.
CORE TARGETS AVAILABLE INSIDE A MAJOR PENTATONIC
I - A major: A root, C# third, E fifth.
IV - D major: F# third, A fifth. The D root is not in A major pentatonic.
V - E major: E root, B fifth. The G# third is not in A major pentatonic.
Module D adds D and G# temporarily as chord-completion tones; they are not new pentatonic degrees.
CHORD-ROLE MATRIX
Note | Over A | Over D | Over E
A over E functions as 11/sus4 tension. C# over D functions as major-7 tension. Use either as motion, not an
unresolved downbeat landing, until the ear clearly hears the intended color.
COUNTS
Module A chord-target cells: 168 notes.
Module B voice-leading routes: 60 held tones.
Module C five position phrases: 160 eighth notes.
Module D chord-completion cadences: 60 quarter notes.
Module E model 12-bar chorus: 48 quarter notes.
Complete written workout: 496 sounding tones before optional articulation overlays.
MODULE A - FIVE-POSITION CHORD-TARGET CELLS
Play every target in the position from low to high, repeat the highest target, then return. Every cell is even.
Practice with D-start and U-start. Say the chord role of every note: root, third, or fifth.
P1 - ROOT FRAME - FRETS 4-7

source_semantic_instructions.practice_and_mastery_text:
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Speak the I-IV-V chord tones and the five-note role matrix.
2. Complete one Position-1 target cell for each chord with both pick starts.
3. Play all fifteen target cells; hear the active chord before each cell.
4. Hold the three voice-leading routes as whole notes in all five positions.
5. Play one four-bar phrase and verify every beat-1 landing.
6. Add all five phrases, then one Level-36 articulation per bar.
7. Add D* and G#* through the five completion cadences.
8. Complete the 12-bar model chorus, then create a new fill while preserving its targets.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
SCALE-RUN AUTOPILOT: stop the fill; play only one whole-note target per chord.
WEAK CHORD CHANGE: sing the next target before the bar arrives; reduce the fill to two notes.
D-CHORD C# LANDING: treat C# as major-7 tension and resolve immediately to D*, B, or a printed strong target.
E-CHORD A LANDING: treat A as suspended 11 tension and resolve to G#*, B, or E.
FRET SEARCH: name the string and fret before leaving the current target.
OVERFILLED BAR: leave beat 4 empty; silence is part of the phrase.
PICK OR ARTICULATION RESET: preserve the target rhythm first; expression is secondary.

MASTERY GATE BEFORE LEVEL 38
Identify the role of every A-major-pentatonic note over A, D, and E; play all fifteen target cells with both pick
starts; perform all three voice-leading routes in all five positions; land every written phrase target on beat 1;
use D and G# only over their supporting chords; complete the 12-bar chorus on two separate days; and improvise one
new chorus whose chord changes remain audible without a backing track.

NEXT LEVEL
Level 38 combines the five positions, horizontal movement, articulation, and I-IV-V targeting into call-and-response
phrasing and controlled improvisation synthesis.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 38
A MAJOR PENTATONIC CALL-AND-RESPONSE PHRASING AND IMPROVISATION SYNTHESIS
FIXED KEY A - FIVE POSITIONS - HARMONY A, D, AND E MAJOR
PURPOSE
Combine the five fixed-key positions, horizontal movement, expressive articulation, and I-IV-V chord targets
into phrases that sound intentional rather than like scale recitation. Build a short call, leave measured space,
answer the active harmony, develop one recognizable motif, and preserve the chord change while moving across the neck.
A MAJOR PENTATONIC
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
I-IV-V chords: A major = A C# E; D major = D F# A; E major = E G# B.
Strong pentatonic targets: A/C#/E over A; F#/A over D; E/B over E.
Completion tones: D* may appear only over D major; G#* may appear only over E major.
PHRASE GRAMMAR
A call states a rhythm and contour, then leaves room. It often ends on degree 2 or 6 rather than a final tonic.
A response may echo the rhythm, reverse the contour, move to a neighboring position, or change the chord target.
Silence is counted. A rest is not lost time; it is part of the phrase. A response should arrive because the harmony

guidance_lines.text: 108 FINGER PERMUTATIONS - LEVEL 4: THREE-STRING RELAY
1+2+1 two-crossing control in standard tuning.
Fifth position: 1=index/fret 5, 2=middle/fret 6, 3=ring/fret 7, 4=pinky/fret 8.
MOVEMENT RULE
For every adjacent three-string group, play code note 1 on the first string, code notes 2-3 on the middle string,
and code note 4 on the third string. The 1+2+1 description refers to note counts, not finger numbers.
Ascend through E/A/D, A/D/G, D/G/B, G/B/e. Descend through e/B/G, B/G/D, G/D/A, D/A/E.
The four-digit code order never changes. There is no string skip or position shift yet.
WHY THIS IS LEVEL 4
Levels 2 and 3 used one adjacent-string crossing per four-note code. Level 4 adds a second crossing.
With a downstroke start, notes 2 and 4 land on upstrokes. With an upstroke start, both land on downstrokes.
Practicing both starts exposes both pick-escape directions while the fretting position remains fixed.
PRACTICE RULE
Use one 12-exercise set per session. Start 10-15 BPM below your clean Level 3 tempo.
Play ASCEND directly into DESCEND, then repeat the entire exercise with the opposite starting pick stroke.
First pass: lightly accent landing notes 2 and 4. Second pass: make all four notes equal in volume and duration.
Use straight 16ths first. Reintroduce triplet and quintuplet groupings only after the crossings are stable.
After three clean loops, add 2 BPM next session. After two errors or rising tension, reduce 4-6 BPM.

NOISY SHIFT: release earlier, move thumb with hand, reduce 4-6 BPM.

global_context.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 12
MAJOR SCALE ONE-FRET NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Play one compact one-octave major-scale shape, move the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every major key. Begin with A major at low-E fret 5, climb to A major at fret 17,
then reverse and return one fret at a time.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A major is the starting rung, not the key of every rung.
A fixed-key A-major exercise in every neck position requires changing the note layout and is a separate later branch.
MAJOR-SCALE FORMULA
Degrees: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
Intervals: whole - whole - half - whole - whole - whole - half
COMPACT ONE-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
A string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4
D string:     R-1, R+1, R+2        Fingers 1,3,4
The four-fret hand frame runs from R-1 through R+2.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
Play degrees 1-2-3-4-5-6-7-8, then 8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1. The octave root is repeated at the turn.
This creates 16 notes, so the next key begins with the same alternate-picking orientation.
D-start: D U D U D U D U | D U D U D U D U
U-start: U D U D U D U D | U D U D U D U D
Do not restart the pick cycle at the scale turn or at the one-fret shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Use 3-4 neighboring rungs at first. Play even eighth notes and pause one beat after every 16-note cell.
During the pause, release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts.
Then remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return to fret 5.
Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, dragged shift noise, or rising tension.
Advance after the complete route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

name the key, play the cell, and continue in either direction. These are variants of Level 12, not separate full levels.

5. Direction: begin selected sessions at fret 17 and descend first.
6. Random entry: choose any root fret from 5-17, name the key, play its cell, and continue either way.
